label: Fruit fly
plain: The fruit fly of the laboratory: 13,814 genes in UniProt's reference proteome, with one protein shown for each. Many of the channels and pumps Cells has laws for have a counterpart of the same family in it.

modelled.text: Cells models a generic cell and a sheet of such cells, not this animal. The sheet is drawn on a wing for the scales only. The wings and the fly are placeholder outlines: nothing at those scales is simulated.

levels.note: The cell drawn is a generic animal cell, as one of a layer; it is not a model of a cell type of the fly. Its shape and its sizes are the picture's choice: six flat sides where it meets its neighbours, about 20 µm across.

notes.text: A generic animal cell, as one of a layer
Its flat-sided shape is the picture's choice

levels.note: The sheet is the one Cells simulates: a single layer of coupled cells. It stands for no particular tissue of the fly.

notes.text: The sheet Cells simulates: a single layer of coupled cells

levels.label: Wing
levels.note: The outline drawn is a fly's two wings, folded back over its body, as a placeholder. The wing is the picture's choice of organ: a visitor knows it, and the project's record names the Drosophila wing disc as a long-term target of its work on how a tissue takes its shape (the user's decisions of 9 November 2026 on the morphogenesis plan). No wing and no wing disc is modelled. The sheet of cells is drawn on a wing so that the scales follow one another; it is not the wing's tissue. Each wing is drawn 2 mm long: the picture's choice, since no measurement was read for this file.

sheet_mark.note: The sheet, to scale: drawn on a wing for the scales only

notes.text: A fly's wings: a placeholder outline
The wing's own cells are not modelled

levels.label: Whole fly
levels.note: The outline drawn is a fruit fly with its wings folded back, 2.5 mm long, as a placeholder. The sheet of cells is drawn on a wing for the scales only. The fly's length, its width and its proportions are the picture's choice: no measurement was read for this file.

notes.text: A fruit fly: a placeholder outline

facts.label: Proteins
facts.value: 13,814 genes in UniProt's reference proteome, with 21,941 entries: 3,885 reviewed by a curator and 18,056 annotated automatically. One protein is shown for each gene

facts.label: Cells' units
facts.value: of the 49 units of the law inventory, 38 have proteins of the same family in the fly and 3 are built from another family; 2 were not found
